title: Any client can read any other company's order by id
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} returns 200 with full order data to a user from a different company; the Client Portal order page shows it too. The orders list is correctly scoped, only the detail lookup is not (OWASP API1:2023).
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 (Acme Traders) and POST /api/orders with reference QA-iso-1 (probe I1); note the returned id
Sign in as bright-1 (Bright Foods) and GET /api/orders/{that id} (probe I3), then as zain-1 (probe I4); see evidence for the exact requests
Also, in the Client Portal as acme-1, open order.html?id=o-1009 (a Bright Foods order) and see it with company name and items
Repeat: same result on the second attempt of each probe
expected: HTTP 403 or 404 with no order data for a user of another company
actual: HTTP 200 with the order, including the QA-iso-1 marker. The portal page 'Order BF-2216' for a Bright Foods order rendered for acme-1. A custom X-Client-Id header made no difference (probe I13).
suspected_cause: The detail handler looks the order up by id without comparing its client_id to the caller's

regression_test.description: Create an order as acme-1, GET it as bright-1 and expect 403/404; GET as acme-2 expects 200

title: Client accounts can list all customers' personal and payment details
summary: GET /api/admin/customers is documented as admin-only (403 for others) but returns 200 for every client account, exposing every company's contact name, email, phone, national ID, address, card details and internal notes (OWASP API5:2023). The role matrix confirms 200 for acme-1, acme-2, bright-1 and zain-1.
steps: Sign in over the API as bright-1
GET /api/admin/customers (probe I11) and again as zain-1 (probe I12)
Observe 200 with a record per company, including other companies' data
Fields exposed (names only): contact_name, email, phone, cnic, address, card_last4, notes (one note contains what looks like a full card number and expiry)
expected: HTTP 403 for any non-admin role (spec lists 403)
suspected_cause: Customers route is missing the admin role check that /admin/reports/sales has

regression_test.description: GET /admin/customers as each client role and expect 403; as admin expect 200

title: Signing out does not end the session: the token keeps working
summary: After POST /api/auth/logout returns 204, the same bearer token still gets 200 on /api/me and /api/orders. The spec says logout revokes the token, and the business rule says signing out ends the session at once. The portal's Sign out only clears browser storage.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-2
POST /api/auth/logout (probe S1) and see 204
With the same token GET /api/me (probe S2) and GET /api/orders (probe S3)
Observe 200 on both, twice each
expected: HTTP 401 for every call with the signed-out token
suspected_cause: Logout does not add the token to a revocation list or the auth middleware does not check one

regression_test.description: Log out, then GET /me with the same token and expect 401

title: Tax is charged on the full subtotal instead of the discounted subtotal
summary: For orders with a subtotal of 1,000.00 or more the 5% discount is applied, but tax is still 10% of the undiscounted subtotal. The rule is tax on the discounted subtotal, so every discounted order is overcharged by 0.5% of the subtotal (5.00 on a 1,000.00 order). Seeded orders show the same pattern.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with reference QA-b2 and items p-102 x 80 (subtotal 1,000.00; probe B2)
Expected discount 50.00, tax 95.00, total 1,045.00; observe tax 100.00, total 1,050.00
Same with p-101 x 156 (probe B3: expected total 1,059.63, got 1,064.70) and p-101 x 1000 (probe B4: expected 6,792.50, got 6,825.00)
In the Client Portal as acme-1 order 80 x Ballpoint Pens: confirmation says Total: $1,050.00; the Admin Portal order page shows Subtotal 1,000.00, Discount -50.00, Tax 100.00, Total 1,050.00
expected: Total 1,045.00 (1,000.00 - 50.00 + 95.00). Below the threshold (998.00, probe B1) the totals are correct.
actual: Total 1,050.00, in the API, both portals and the CSV export; the discount is applied but tax is computed before it
suspected_cause: tax_cents is computed from subtotal_cents rather than subtotal_cents - discount_cents

regression_test.description: Order of exactly 100000 cents expects discount 5000, tax 9500, total 104500; 101400 cents expects total 105963

title: Order quantity limits are not enforced: 0, 1001, 1.5 and an empty item list are accepted
summary: POST /api/orders returns 201 for quantity 0, 1001 and 1.5 and for an empty items array, although the spec and rules say whole numbers 1 to 1,000 and at least one item. The Client Portal form accepts quantity 0 too and shows 'Order QA-ui-q0 placed. Total: $0.00.'
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items [] (probe P043), then with items[0].quantity 0, 1001 and 1.5 (probes P044, P045, P046)
Observe 201 each time
In the Client Portal as acme-1 open New order, enter reference QA-ui-q0, choose A4 Copy Paper, quantity 0, click Place order, and see a $0.00 order created
expected: HTTP 400 naming the field; the form should refuse too
actual: HTTP 201 and orders stored (zero-value orders, quantity 1001 and 1.5). Quantity 1000 and a string quantity '5' behave correctly.
suspected_cause: No range or integer check on quantity and no minimum on items in the order handler or the form

regression_test.description: POST orders with items [], quantity 0, 1001 and 1.5 and expect 400 each

title: The same order submitted twice at once creates two orders
summary: Two identical POST /api/orders sent in parallel both return 201 and two orders with the same reference and items are stored. Nothing in the spec allows duplicates or offers an idempotency key. I am unsure the product intends one order per click, so severity follows user impact (double billing).
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
Send two identical POST /api/orders in parallel (probe P049)
Observe two 201 responses; GET /api/orders lists two QA-reference orders created in the same millisecond (o-1025 and o-1026)
expected: One order, or a clear duplicate refusal (409)
suspected_cause: No de-duplication or idempotency handling on order creation

regression_test.description: Send two identical parallel POST /orders and expect exactly one order created

title: Order search with ( or \ and page_size=0 crash the server (HTTP 500); negative page_size accepted
summary: GET /api/orders?q=( and q=\ return 500, probably an unescaped regular expression. page_size=0 returns 500 and page_size=-1 returns 200 with page_size -1 although the spec minimum is 1 (400 expected). In the Admin Portal, typing ( in the search box shows 'Could not load orders (500).' and leaves the previous list on screen.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 (or admin) and GET /api/orders?q=( (probe P024), q=\ (P028), page_size=0 (P019), page_size=-1 (P020)
Observe 500, 500, 500 and 200
In the Admin Portal as admin, open Orders, type ( in Search and press Enter: the page shows 'Could not load orders (500).' and the console shows the failed request
expected: Special characters are searched literally (200); invalid page_size gives 400
actual: HTTP 500 for q=( , q=\ and page_size=0; 200 with an invalid echoed page_size for -1
suspected_cause: The query string is passed to new RegExp without escaping and page_size is not range-checked

regression_test.description: GET /orders?q=( expects 200 with an empty list; page_size=0 and -1 expect 400

title: Malformed JSON requests return a stack trace and server file paths
summary: Sending invalid JSON to POST /api/auth/login (and POST /api/orders) gives a 400 whose body contains a stack trace, a stack field and server source file paths.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with the raw body {bad json (probe P007), anonymous or any role
POST /api/orders with malformed JSON as acme-1 (probe P048)
Read the response body in the evidence: stack trace and file paths present both times
expected: A short 400 error naming the problem, no internals
actual: 400 with stack trace and absolute server paths
suspected_cause: The default error handler returns the error stack to the client

regression_test.description: POST malformed JSON and expect a 400 body without 'stack' or file paths

title: Urdu order notes and company names display reversed on the order detail page
summary: On the order page the Company and Note values (class text-cell) use unicode-bidi: bidi-override with direction ltr, so Urdu letters are shown in reverse order and unconnected. The note 'ہنگامی آرڈر، آج ہی بھیجیں' reads as scrambled text, and the title 'Order زین-1044' shows the number before the dash. The header and order list show the same Urdu correctly.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as zain-1 in a fresh profile
Open My orders and click View on the first order (زین-1044, order id o-1012)
Compare the Company and Note rows with the same text in the page header and the orders list
In the browser check the computed style of #o-note: unicode-bidi bidi-override, direction ltr
Reload the page and check again
expected: Urdu text right-to-left and readable (dir=auto or bdi, no bidi-override)
actual: Letters reversed ('زرڈیرٹ نیز' for 'زین ٹریڈرز'); both reproduced after reload
suspected_cause: CSS rule on .text-cell forces bidi-override and ltr

regression_test.description: Render order page for the Urdu order and assert #o-note computed unicode-bidi is not bidi-override

title: On a phone the New order form runs off screen and the Place order button is out of view
summary: At 390px wide the page is 555px wide: the reference and note fields, the quantity box, the Remove button and Place order start or end outside the screen. Place order begins at x=435 on a 390px screen, so a client must scroll sideways to place an order.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal (acme-1, then again bright-1 in a fresh profile)
Resize to 390x844
Open New order and run the page audit or look at the screenshot
The page scrolls sideways by 165px; input fields are cut off on the right and Place order is off screen
expected: All fields and Place order fit within the width
actual: Controls pushed 45 to 165px outside the viewport
suspected_cause: Fixed-width form rows (item row with select, quantity and Remove) force the card wider than the screen

regression_test.description: At 390px width, assert the document scroll width equals the viewport width on new-order.html

title: My orders on mobile: first row sits under the toolbar and Total and View are hidden in a scroll box
summary: At 390px the orders table (457px wide) scrolls inside a 359px box with no visible cue, so the Total is clipped and the View link is out of sight. The first row overlaps the toolbar (New order button) by about 22px.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1, resize to 390x844
Open My orders, look at the first row and the right edge of the table
Reload and measure: the table's scrollWidth is 457 and its box is 359; first row top is 241px, toolbar bottom 263px
expected: Row clear of the toolbar; key columns reachable or a visible scroll cue
suspected_cause: Table wrapper with overflow auto and no spacing below the sticky or floated toolbar

regression_test.description: At 390px assert the first order row does not intersect the toolbar

title: The product selector on the New order form has no accessible name
summary: The product dropdown has no label, so a screen reader announces it only as a combobox and the page audit lists it as an unnamed control.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal and open New order
Read the page snapshot: combobox with no name next to the Quantity spinbutton (named)
Run the audit: unnamedControls lists select[name=product]; same result for bright-1 in a fresh profile
expected: A label such as 'Product' for each line
suspected_cause: Select rendered without label or aria-label

regression_test.description: Assert every select on new-order.html has an accessible name

title: Sales report takes about 4 seconds to answer
summary: GET /api/admin/reports/sales consistently takes 4.0 to 4.2 seconds while other calls take a few milliseconds. The Admin Portal Reports page shows only the heading until it arrives.
steps: Sign in as admin over the API
GET /api/admin/reports/sales (probes P061, P093, E6)
Observe 4004 to 4226 ms each time
expected: A response in well under 3 seconds, or a loading indicator on the page
actual: About 4 seconds on every call (6 of 6)
suspected_cause: A deliberate delay or an unindexed aggregation in the report handler

regression_test.description: Time GET /admin/reports/sales and expect under 1500 ms on the seeded data
